papers.title: Association between post-vaccination adverse events and subsequent COVID-19 booster uptake in the Netherlands.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to assess whether the occurrence, severity, and duration of AE following COVID-19 booster vaccination were associated with subsequent booster uptake during the 2022-2024 autumn booster campaigns in the Netherlands. METHODS: We included participants from the Vaccine Study COVID-19 (VASCO), an ongoing prospective cohort study, who were eligible for booster vaccination in 2022-2024. Participants completed a questionnaire on AE one month after booster vaccination. Logistic regression was performed to assess the association between the occurrence, severity, and duration of local and systemic AE, and revaccination during the subsequent year. We adjusted for demographics and prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. RESULTS: In 2022 and 2023, 11,010 and 14,824 participants were vaccinated and completed the AE questionnaire. Of these, 73.7% and 87.0% were revaccinated in subsequent years. The occurrence of systemic AE in 2022 was associated with a lower odds of revaccination in 2023 (OR: 0.84 [95%CI, 0.76-0.93]). The likelihood of revaccination declined with increasing severity- moderate (0.79 [0.66-0.94]) and severe AE (0.45 [0.34-0.60]) - and longer duration (>5 days: 0.72 [0.54-0.95]) of systemic AE. Also, severe local AE (0.38 [0.23-0.60]) and seeking medical care for AE (0.50 [0.34-0.73]) were associated with reduced vaccination uptake. Similar associations were observed for revaccination in 2024. CONCLUSION: This study found a lower likelihood of subsequent COVID-19 booster uptake after experiencing systemic AE, particularly when severe or prolonged, or when experiencing a severe local AE. These findings underscore the need to address experienced AE in communication strategies, as this may influence the success of vaccination campaigns.

papers.title_zh: Association between post-vaccination adverse events and subsequent COVID-19 booster uptake in the Netherlands.
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to assess whether the occurrence, severity, and duration of AE following COVID-19 booster vaccination were associated with subsequent booster uptake during the 2022-2024 autumn booster campaigns in the Netherlands. METHODS: We included participants from the Vaccine Study COVID-19 (VASCO), an ongoing prospective cohort study, who were eligible for booster vaccination in 2022-2024. Participants completed a questionnaire on AE one month after booster vaccination. Logistic regression was performed to assess the association between the occurrence, severity, and duration of local and systemic AE, and revaccination during the subsequent year. We adjusted for demographics and prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. RESULTS: In 2022 and 2023, 11,010 and 14,824 participants were vaccinated and completed the AE questionnaire. Of these, 73.7% and 87.0% were revaccinated in subsequent years. The occurrence of systemic AE in 2022 was associated with a lower odds of revaccination in 2023 (OR: 0.84 [95%CI, 0.76-0.93]). The likelihood of revaccination declined with increasing severity- moderate (0.79 [0.66-0.94]) and severe AE (0.45 [0.34-0.60]) - and longer duration (>5 days: 0.72 [0.54-0.95]) of systemic AE. Also, severe local AE (0.38 [0.23-0.60]) and seeking medical care for AE (0.50 [0.34-0.73]) were associated with reduced vaccination uptake. Similar associations were observed for revaccination in 2024. CONCLUSION: This study found a lower likelihood of subsequent COVID-19 booster uptake after experiencing systemic AE, particularly when severe or prolonged, or when experiencing a severe local AE. These findings underscore the need to address experienced AE in communication strategies, as this may influence the success of vaccination campaigns.

papers.title: Emergence of COVID-19 variant XFG not linked to higher rates of sore throat or altered severity: Evidence from participatory surveillance in the Netherlands.
papers.abstract: Here, we investigate symptoms linked to the new SARS-CoV-2 variant XFG using an evidence-based method to determine possible elevated levels of sore throat and severity as suggested by on-line news reports and social media. Participants (n = 39,937) in the participatory surveillance program, Infectieradar, weekly report respiratory symptoms and severity of disease. In addition, SARS-CoV-2 self-test results are reported and a representative subsample of all participants with symptoms sent a nose-throat swab for molecular diagnostic testing and sequencing. We compared symptom prevalence, symptom burden and severity of disease in week 28 to week 40 in 2025, when SARS-CoV-2 strain XFG was dominant, with the same period in 2024, in which the KP.3 variant was most abundant. We compared these two periods through adjusted odds ratios and estimated marginal means to provide evidence for possibly altered symptomatology or disease severity. Sore throat was not significantly higher during the COVID-19 wave in 2025, compared to 2024, nor were any other symptoms. Additionally, the number of symptoms and severity of disease in the two periods is comparable. We conclude that sore throat is not indicative for the emerging XFG variant, nor that worse severity of disease is experienced during current COVID-19 cases in the general population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate whether the emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 variant XFG was associated with higher rates of sore throat or altered disease severity, as suggested by online news reports and social media.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A participatory surveillance program, Infectieradar, collected weekly reports of respiratory symptoms and disease severity from 39,937 participants in the Netherlands during two specific periods in 2024 and 2025.
analysis.methods: Participants reported SARS-CoV-2 self-test results and a representative subsample with symptoms underwent molecular diagnostic testing and sequencing. Symptom prevalence, burden, and severity were compared between the two periods using adjusted odds ratios and estimated marginal means.
analysis.main_results: Sore throat was not significantly higher during the 2025 wave compared to 2024, and no other symptoms showed significant differences. The number of symptoms and disease severity in the two periods were comparable.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that sore throat is not indicative of the XFG variant and that disease severity during the 2025 wave was not worse than in 2024, based on the comparison of symptomatology and severity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the XFG variant does not cause a notable increase in sore throat or disease severity, which may inform public health surveillance and clinical expectations during future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on self-reported data and does not include laboratory confirmation for all cases, which may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate due to the reliance on observational data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether the emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 variant XFG was associated with higher rates of sore throat or altered disease severity. Using data from the participatory surveillance program Infectieradar, the researchers compared symptom prevalence and disease severity between two periods in 2024 and 2025 when the KP.3 and XFG variants were dominant, respectively. They found no significant increase in sore throat or other symptoms during the XFG wave, and disease severity was comparable to the KP.3 period. The authors concluded that XFG does not appear to be linked to increased sore throat or worse disease severity. The study's findings may inform public health surveillance and clinical expectations, but the reliance on self-reported data and lack of comprehensive laboratory confirmation limit the strength of the evidence.

papers.title: Effect of Regional COVID-19 Lockdowns on Alcohol Use and Smoking in Two Chilean University Communities: A Difference-In-Difference Analysis.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Effects of lockdowns on alcohol use and smoking remain unclear. By exploiting the variation in regional COVID-19 lockdowns in two Chilean regions, we examined their effect on alcohol use and smoking in two university communities. METHODS: We conducted a quasi-experimental study in university communities in two Chilean regions, Coquimbo and Araucanía. Participants were a longitudinal cohort (n = 896) assessed seven times from July 2020 ( t 1 ) to April 2021 ( t 7 ). Outcomes were weekly grams of alcohol use, heavy episodic drinking (HED) and cigarettes smoked per day. RESULTS: Lockdown between t 1 and t 3 was associated with an increase of 15.6 g of alcohol used per week (95% confidence interval 1.8; 29.3) and an increase of 0.3 daily cigarettes smoked (95% confidence interval 0.003; 0.5) at t 3 (September 2020), compared to the absence of lockdown. When lockdown reversed at t 5 , we found weak evidence of a reduction in alcohol use and smoking in the region under lockdown. We did not observe changes in HED during the study period. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 lockdown appears to result in an initial relative increase in weekly volume of alcohol use and cigarette smoking compared to a region affected by the COVID-19 pandemic but without lockdown. We did not find evidence of changes in HED. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT05069090.

source_records.title: Effect of Regional COVID‐19 Lockdowns on Alcohol Use and Smoking in Two Chilean University Communities: A Difference‐In‐Difference Analysis
source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Effects of lockdowns on alcohol use and smoking remain unclear. By exploiting the variation in regional COVID‐19 lockdowns in two Chilean regions, we examined their effect on alcohol use and smoking in two university communities. Methods We conducted a quasi‐experimental study in university communities in two Chilean regions, Coquimbo and Araucanía. Participants were a longitudinal cohort (n = 896) assessed seven times from July 2020 (t1) to April 2021 (t7). Outcomes were weekly grams of alcohol use, heavy episodic drinking (HED) and cigarettes smoked per day. Results Lockdown between t1 and t3 was associated with an increase of 15.6 g of alcohol used per week (95% confidence interval 1.8; 29.3) and an increase of 0.3 daily cigarettes smoked (95% confidence interval 0.003; 0.5) at t3 (September 2020), compared to the absence of lockdown. When lockdown reversed at t5, we found weak evidence of a reduction in alcohol use and smoking in the region under lockdown. We did not observe changes in HED during the study period. Discussion and Conclusions COVID‐19 lockdown appears to result in an initial relative increase in weekly volume of alcohol use and cigarette smoking compared to a region affected by the COVID‐19 pandemic but without lockdown. We did not find evidence of changes in HED. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT05069090

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of regional COVID-19 lockdowns on alcohol use and smoking behaviors in two Chilean university communities using a difference-in-difference analysis. A longitudinal cohort of 896 participants was assessed seven times between July 2020 and April 2021. The results indicated an initial increase in alcohol consumption and cigarette smoking during the first lockdown period, with weak evidence of a reduction when lockdowns were reversed. No changes in heavy episodic drinking were observed. The study suggests that lockdowns may influence substance use behaviors, which could inform public health strategies during pandemics. However, the evidence is limited by the study design and the lack of detailed information on limitations.

papers.title: A Retrospective Cohort Study: Neonatal survey of pregnant women infected with SARS-CoV-2 during pregnancy
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection increases risks of adverse outcomes in pregnancy. However, comprehensive data on neonatal health following maternal infection remain limited. Objectives To compare maternal complications and neonatal outcomes between SARS-CoV-2-infected and uninfected pregnant women. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of pregnant women with and without laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. Maternal complications and neonatal physical indicators/diseases were systematically analyzed (significance: p Results Maternal outcomes: SARS-CoV-2-infected women had significantly higher complication rates vs. uninfected controls (p 0.05). Term and preterm infants of infected mothers showed elevated incidences of: myocardial enzyme pattern abnormalities, neonatal pneumonia, central atrial septal defect, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, neonatal clotting diseases, neonatal respiratory failure (p Conclusions Maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection significantly increases preterm birth risk and neonatal morbidity. First-trimester exposure may drive late-pregnancy complications. These findings underscore the need for enhanced prenatal surveillance and long-term offspring follow-up.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health concern that SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy may elevate risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, noting that comprehensive neonatal health data following maternal infection remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study compared pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection to uninfected controls, systematically analyzing maternal complications and neonatal outcomes.
analysis.methods: The authors retrospectively identified SARS-CoV-2-infected and uninfected pregnant women and systematically analyzed maternal complications and neonatal physical indicators and diseases using standard clinical assessments.
analysis.main_results: SARS-CoV-2-infected women had significantly higher complication rates than uninfected controls, and their term and preterm infants showed elevated incidences of myocardial enzyme pattern abnormalities, neonatal pneumonia, central atrial septal defect, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, neonatal clotting diseases, and neonatal respiratory failure.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection significantly increases preterm birth risk and neonatal morbidity, with first-trimester exposure potentially driving late-pregnancy complications.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support enhanced prenatal surveillance and long-term offspring follow-up to mitigate risks associated with maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design and reliance on abstract-only evidence limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting moderate confidence in the reported associations.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study assessed maternal and neonatal outcomes among pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to uninfected controls. Infected women experienced higher complication rates, and their infants showed increased incidences of myocardial enzyme abnormalities, neonatal pneumonia, central atrial septal defect, hyperbilirubinemia, clotting diseases, and respiratory failure. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection elevates preterm birth risk and neonatal morbidity, with potential late-pregnancy complications linked to first-trimester exposure. The study recommends enhanced prenatal surveillance and long-term offspring follow-up. However, the retrospective design and abstract-only evidence constrain causal conclusions and generalizability, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.main_results: 感染严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的妇女的并发症发生率显着高于未感染对照,其足月和早产儿的心肌酶模式异常、新生儿肺炎、中心房间隔缺损、新生儿高胆红素血症、新生儿凝血疾病和新生儿呼吸衰竭的发病率升高。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health concern that SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy may elevate risks for adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, noting that comprehensive neonatal health data following maternal infection remain limited.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study compared pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection to uninfected controls, systematically analyzing maternal complications and neonatal outcomes.
analysis_en.methods: The authors retrospectively identified SARS-CoV-2-infected and uninfected pregnant women and systematically analyzed maternal complications and neonatal physical indicators and diseases using standard clinical assessments.
analysis_en.main_results: SARS-CoV-2-infected women had significantly higher complication rates than uninfected controls, and their term and preterm infants showed elevated incidences of myocardial enzyme pattern abnormalities, neonatal pneumonia, central atrial septal defect, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, neonatal clotting diseases, and neonatal respiratory failure.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection significantly increases preterm birth risk and neonatal morbidity, with first-trimester exposure potentially driving late-pregnancy complications.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support enhanced prenatal surveillance and long-term offspring follow-up to mitigate risks associated with maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The retrospective design and reliance on abstract-only evidence limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting moderate confidence in the reported associations.

papers.title: 2024-2025 BNT162b2 KP.2 COVID-19 full season vaccine effectiveness from vaccine registries linked to administrative claims in two states: A cohort study in non-immunocompromised adults.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Data on effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccinations during the 2024-2025 respiratory season are limited, particularly among those with underlying medical conditions (UMC). We estimated BNT162b2 KP.2 vaccine effectiveness (VE) against COVID-19-associated hospital admission, emergency department (ED), and urgent care (UC) visits in two U.S. METHODS Retrospective cohort study of non-immunocompromised adults living in Louisiana or California, with ≥1 year prior continuous enrollment in insurance plans contributing to the HealthVerity claims database beginning August 22, 2024. The effectiveness of BNT162b2 KP.2 vaccine (2024-2025 formulation, hereafter referred to as BNT162b2), measured as a time-varying exposure against hospital admission, ED, or UC encounters with International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) code U07.1 was calculated as 1 - adjusted hazard ratio using Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age group, sex, state, insurance payor, presence or absence of UMCs, and pre-index healthcare utilization. Stratifications included those aged 65 years and older, those aged 18-64 years with UMCs, and those aged 18-64 years without UMCs. RESULTS The cohort included 6,256,421 individuals (93% California, 7% Louisiana); 330,565 (5%) received the BNT162b2 vaccine. Vaccinated individuals were older and had more comorbidities, wellness visits, and prior influenza vaccination. Overall, 66% of the study population had ≥1 UMC; the most prevalent conditions were obesity (25%), history of immunocompromised conditions (23%), and mental health conditions (19%). COVID-19-related encounter rates for ED, UC or hospitalization were lower among vaccinated compared to unvaccinated persons (25.1 vs 36.3 per 100,000 person-months). Among all adults, VE was 37% against hospitalization, 12% against ED/UC encounters, and 16% against ED/UC/hospitalization encounters. Results were similar across age groups and UMCs. CONCLUSIONS BNT162b2 provided protection against COVID-19-associated outcomes of ED, UC or hospitalization among non-immunocompromised U.S. adults, including those with UMCs, over the course of the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season, supporting continued vaccine recommendations. REGISTRATION This study was posted on clinicaltrials.gov prior to analyses (NCT06923137).

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the effectiveness of the BNT162b2 KP.2 vaccine against COVID-19-associated hospital admissions, emergency department visits, and urgent care encounters during the 2024-2025 respiratory season, as data on this topic are limited, especially among individuals with underlying medical conditions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among non-immunocompromised adults in Louisiana and California, with ≥1 year of prior continuous insurance enrollment in the HealthVerity claims database starting August 22, 2024. The cohort included 6,256,421 individuals, of whom 330,565 (5%) received the BNT162b2 vaccine.
analysis.methods: The study used a time-varying exposure approach to calculate vaccine effectiveness against hospital admission, emergency department, or urgent care encounters using ICD-10-CM code U07.1. Adjusted hazard ratios were estimated via Cox proportional hazard models, accounting for age group, sex, state, insurance payor, presence or absence of underlying medical conditions, and prior healthcare utilization.
analysis.main_results: The effectiveness of BNT162b2 against hospitalization was 37%, against emergency department/urgent care encounters was 12%, and against all three outcomes combined was 16%. These results were consistent across age groups and underlying medical conditions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the BNT162b2 vaccine provided protection against COVID-19-associated outcomes, including hospitalization, emergency department, and urgent care visits, among non-immunocompromised U.S. adults during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support continued vaccine recommendations for non-immunocompromised adults, including those with underlying medical conditions, during the 2024-2025 respiratory season, highlighting the vaccine's role in reducing severe outcomes of COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its reliance on administrative claims data, which may introduce biases and missing information. However, the evidence is strong, with a large cohort size and adjustment for multiple confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of the BNT162b2 KP.2 vaccine against COVID-19-associated hospital admissions, emergency department visits, and urgent care encounters during the 2024-2025 respiratory season in non-immunocompromised adults in Louisiana and California. The analysis used a retrospective cohort design, linking vaccine registries to administrative claims data. Vaccine effectiveness was calculated using Cox proportional hazard models, adjusting for age, sex, state, insurance payor, underlying medical conditions, and prior healthcare utilization. The results showed 37% effectiveness against hospitalization, 12% against emergency department/urgent care encounters, and 16% against all three outcomes combined. These findings were consistent across age groups and underlying medical conditions, supporting continued vaccine recommendations. The study's large cohort size and comprehensive adjustments enhance the reliability of the results, though reliance on claims data may introduce biases. The evidence is strong, with no significant limitations reported.

elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用时变暴露方法,使用 ICD-10-CM 代码 U07.1 计算 疫苗 对入院、急诊室或紧急护理遭遇的有效性。调整后的风险比是通过 Cox 比例风险模型估计的,考虑了年龄组、性别、州、保险支付人、是否存在潜在的医疗状况以及之前的医疗保健利用情况。
elements_zh.main_results: BNT162b2 对抗住院治疗的有效性为 37%,对抗急诊室/紧急护理的有效性为 12%,对抗所有三种结局的有效性为 16%。这些结果在不同年龄组和基础健康状况下是一致的。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the BNT162b2 vaccine provided protection against COVID-19-associated outcomes, including hospitalization, emergency department, and urgent care visits, among non-immunocompromised U.S. adults during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support continued vaccine recommendations for non-immunocompromised adults, including those with underlying medical conditions, during the 2024-2025 respiratory season, highlighting the vaccine's role in reducing severe outcomes of COVID-19.

analysis_en.methods: The study used a time-varying exposure approach to calculate vaccine effectiveness against hospital admission, emergency department, or urgent care encounters using ICD-10-CM code U07.1. Adjusted hazard ratios were estimated via Cox proportional hazard models, accounting for age group, sex, state, insurance payor, presence or absence of underlying medical conditions, and prior healthcare utilization.
analysis_en.main_results: The effectiveness of BNT162b2 against hospitalization was 37%, against emergency department/urgent care encounters was 12%, and against all three outcomes combined was 16%. These results were consistent across age groups and underlying medical conditions.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the BNT162b2 vaccine provided protection against COVID-19-associated outcomes, including hospitalization, emergency department, and urgent care visits, among non-immunocompromised U.S. adults during the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support continued vaccine recommendations for non-immunocompromised adults, including those with underlying medical conditions, during the 2024-2025 respiratory season, highlighting the vaccine's role in reducing severe outcomes of COVID-19.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its reliance on administrative claims data, which may introduce biases and missing information. However, the evidence is strong, with a large cohort size and adjustment for multiple confounding factors.

papers.title_zh: 2024-2025 BNT162b2 KP.2 COVID-19 full season vaccine effectiveness from vaccine registries linked to administrative claims in two states: A cohort study in non-immunocompromised adults.
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Data on effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccinations during the 2024-2025 respiratory season are limited, particularly among those with underlying medical conditions (UMC). We estimated BNT162b2 KP.2 vaccine effectiveness (VE) against COVID-19-associated hospital admission, emergency department (ED), and urgent care (UC) visits in two U.S. METHODS Retrospective cohort study of non-immunocompromised adults living in Louisiana or California, with ≥1 year prior continuous enrollment in insurance plans contributing to the HealthVerity claims database beginning August 22, 2024. The effectiveness of BNT162b2 KP.2 vaccine (2024-2025 formulation, hereafter referred to as BNT162b2), measured as a time-varying exposure against hospital admission, ED, or UC encounters with International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) code U07.1 was calculated as 1 - adjusted hazard ratio using Cox proportional hazard models adjusted for age group, sex, state, insurance payor, presence or absence of UMCs, and pre-index healthcare utilization. Stratifications included those aged 65 years and older, those aged 18-64 years with UMCs, and those aged 18-64 years without UMCs. RESULTS The cohort included 6,256,421 individuals (93% California, 7% Louisiana); 330,565 (5%) received the BNT162b2 vaccine. Vaccinated individuals were older and had more comorbidities, wellness visits, and prior influenza vaccination. Overall, 66% of the study population had ≥1 UMC; the most prevalent conditions were obesity (25%), history of immunocompromised conditions (23%), and mental health conditions (19%). COVID-19-related encounter rates for ED, UC or hospitalization were lower among vaccinated compared to unvaccinated persons (25.1 vs 36.3 per 100,000 person-months). Among all adults, VE was 37% against hospitalization, 12% against ED/UC encounters, and 16% against ED/UC/hospitalization encounters. Results were similar across age groups and UMCs. CONCLUSIONS BNT162b2 provided protection against COVID-19-associated outcomes of ED, UC or hospitalization among non-immunocompromised U.S. adults, including those with UMCs, over the course of the 2024-2025 respiratory virus season, supporting continued vaccine recommendations. REGISTRATION This study was posted on clinicaltrials.gov prior to analyses (NCT06923137).

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性 队列研究 研究在路易斯安那州和加利福尼亚州的非免疫功能低下成年人中进行,自 2024 年 8 月 22 日起,在 HealthVerity 索赔数据库中连续投保≥1 年。队列研究 包括 6,256,421 人,其中 330,565 人 (5%) 接受了 BNT162b2 疫苗。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用时变暴露方法,使用 ICD-10-CM 代码 U07.1 计算 疫苗 对入院、急诊室或紧急护理遭遇的有效性。调整后的风险比是通过 Cox 比例风险模型估计的,考虑了年龄组、性别、州、保险支付人、是否存在潜在的医疗状况以及之前的医疗保健利用情况。
analysis_zh.main_results: BNT162b2 对抗住院治疗的有效性为 37%,对抗急诊室/紧急护理的有效性为 12%,对抗所有三种结局的有效性为 16%。这些结果在不同年龄组和基础健康状况下是一致的。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对行政索赔数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏见和信息缺失。然而,证据是强有力的,队列研究 的大小很大,并且对多个混杂因素进行了调整。

papers.title: Infection prevention and control adherence among SARS-CoV-2 infected healthcare workers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: lessons for future outbreaks.
papers.abstract: Background Health care worker (HCW) infections during outbreaks of high-consequence pathogens, from SARS-CoV-2 to Ethiopia's 2025-2026 Marburg outbreak, highlight persistent Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) gaps. We evaluated IPC adherence and its determinants among infected HCWs in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to inform future outbreak preparedness. Methods This census-based cross-sectional study (March 2020-March 2021) evaluated 1152 SARS-CoV-2-infected HCWs with clinical exposures 14 days pre-diagnosis. Environments were classified via an adapted OSHA pyramid into: High-Pathogen Designated Areas isolation and treatment units, General High-Risk Areas [intensive care units, emergency departments, and operating theaters], Medium-Risk Clinical Areas [inpatient and outpatient departments], and Low-Risk Support Areas [administrative and non-clinical zones]. Adherence was defined as correct practice in > 50% of interactions. Bivariate chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression identified independent determinants for donning/doffing (n = 742) and N95 seal-checks (n = 350), reporting adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals at P Results Only 19.2% of infected HCWs worked in High-Pathogen Designated Areas. Mask (85.7-97.7%) and glove (68.2-98.0%) adherence was high, but fell below 50% for gowns, coveralls, head caps, and shoe covers. Exceptions included face shields/goggles (52.8%) and N95 use during aerosol-generating procedures (AGPs) (66.5%). N95 seal-check compliance was 34.9%; only 1.1% used fit-tested respirators. Hand hygiene rose from 49.3% pre-interaction to 82.5% post-fluid exposure. Chi-square analyses linked health care professionasl and High-Pathogen Designated Area status with significantly superior adherence. For donning/doffing, lower compliance was predicted by non-High-Pathogen Designated Area placement (General High-Risk Areas aOR = 0.12 (0.07-0.19); Medium-Risk Clinical Areas aOR = 0.08 (0.04-0.14); Low-Risk Support Areas [aOR = 0.07 (0.03-0.17)] and support staff [aOR = 0.35 (0.14-0.88)]; AGP involvement [aOR = 3.61 (2.33-5.58)] and IPC training [aOR = 1.59 (1.05-2.41)] were positive predictors. N95 seal-check odds were lower in General High-Risk Areas aOR = 0.53 (0.30-0.93); Medium-Risk Clinical Areas aOR = 0.33 (0.16-0.66); Low-Risk Support Areas [aOR = 0.25 (0.08-0.77)]. Positive predictors included communal living [aOR = 2.37 (1.29-4.35)], IPC training [aOR = 1.71 (1.03-2.83)], and AGP involvement [aOR = 1.71 (1.05-2.80)], while age > 30 [aOR = 0.57 (0.34-0.98)] and stress [aOR = 0.46 (0.28-0.77)] were negative determinants. Conclusions This study underscores IPC gaps among HCWs especially in non-designated areas, where most infections occurred, highlighting the need for standardized IPC across all healthcare environments.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed infection prevention and control (IPC) adherence among SARS-CoV-2-infected healthcare workers (HCWs) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, during the 2020-2021 pandemic. The research aimed to identify determinants of IPC adherence to improve future outbreak preparedness. A census-based cross-sectional design was used, evaluating 1152 HCWs with clinical exposures 14 days before diagnosis. The study found that only 19.2% of infected HCWs worked in High-Pathogen Designated Areas, highlighting IPC gaps in non-designated areas where most infections occurred. Adherence to masks and gloves was high, but compliance with gowns, coveralls, head caps, and shoe covers fell below 50%. The study classified environments using an adapted OSHA pyramid, emphasizing the need for standardized IPC across all healthcare settings. The findings suggest that factors such as healthcare profession and exposure to aerosol-generating procedures significantly influence adherence, while IPC training and communal living showed positive associations. The study does not report limitations or evidence strength, but its results provide important insights into improving IPC practices during future outbreaks.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们评估了埃塞俄比亚亚的斯亚贝巴受感染医护人员的 IPC 依从性及其决定因素,为未来的 暴发 准备工作提供信息。
elements_zh.methods: 这项基于人口普查的横断面研究(2020 年 3 月至 2021 年 3 月)评估了 1152 名感染 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的医护人员,他们在 诊断 发生前 14 天有临床暴露。
elements_zh.main_results: 只有 19.2% 的受感染医护人员在高病原体指定区域工作。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 遵守被定义为在超过 50% 的互动中采取正确的做法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过改编的 OSHA 金字塔将环境分为:高病原体指定区域隔离和 治疗 单位、一般高风险区域 [重症监护室、急诊科和手术室]、中风险临床区域 [住院和门诊部门] 和低风险支持区域 [行政和非临床区域]。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性或证据强度。

papers.title_zh: 埃塞俄比亚亚的斯亚贝巴市医务人员对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染的预防与控制措施依从性:暴发的未来防控启示
papers.source_body_en: Background Health care worker (HCW) infections during outbreaks of high-consequence pathogens, from SARS-CoV-2 to Ethiopia's 2025-2026 Marburg outbreak, highlight persistent Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) gaps. We evaluated IPC adherence and its determinants among infected HCWs in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to inform future outbreak preparedness. Methods This census-based cross-sectional study (March 2020-March 2021) evaluated 1152 SARS-CoV-2-infected HCWs with clinical exposures 14 days pre-diagnosis. Environments were classified via an adapted OSHA pyramid into: High-Pathogen Designated Areas isolation and treatment units, General High-Risk Areas [intensive care units, emergency departments, and operating theaters], Medium-Risk Clinical Areas [inpatient and outpatient departments], and Low-Risk Support Areas [administrative and non-clinical zones]. Adherence was defined as correct practice in > 50% of interactions. Bivariate chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression identified independent determinants for donning/doffing (n = 742) and N95 seal-checks (n = 350), reporting adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals at P Results Only 19.2% of infected HCWs worked in High-Pathogen Designated Areas. Mask (85.7-97.7%) and glove (68.2-98.0%) adherence was high, but fell below 50% for gowns, coveralls, head caps, and shoe covers. Exceptions included face shields/goggles (52.8%) and N95 use during aerosol-generating procedures (AGPs) (66.5%). N95 seal-check compliance was 34.9%; only 1.1% used fit-tested respirators. Hand hygiene rose from 49.3% pre-interaction to 82.5% post-fluid exposure. Chi-square analyses linked health care professionasl and High-Pathogen Designated Area status with significantly superior adherence. For donning/doffing, lower compliance was predicted by non-High-Pathogen Designated Area placement (General High-Risk Areas aOR = 0.12 (0.07-0.19); Medium-Risk Clinical Areas aOR = 0.08 (0.04-0.14); Low-Risk Support Areas [aOR = 0.07 (0.03-0.17)] and support staff [aOR = 0.35 (0.14-0.88)]; AGP involvement [aOR = 3.61 (2.33-5.58)] and IPC training [aOR = 1.59 (1.05-2.41)] were positive predictors. N95 seal-check odds were lower in General High-Risk Areas aOR = 0.53 (0.30-0.93); Medium-Risk Clinical Areas aOR = 0.33 (0.16-0.66); Low-Risk Support Areas [aOR = 0.25 (0.08-0.77)]. Positive predictors included communal living [aOR = 2.37 (1.29-4.35)], IPC training [aOR = 1.71 (1.03-2.83)], and AGP involvement [aOR = 1.71 (1.05-2.80)], while age > 30 [aOR = 0.57 (0.34-0.98)] and stress [aOR = 0.46 (0.28-0.77)] were negative determinants. Conclusions This study underscores IPC gaps among HCWs especially in non-designated areas, where most infections occurred, highlighting the need for standardized IPC across all healthcare environments.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 从 暴发 到埃塞俄比亚 2025-2026 年马尔堡 暴发,医护人员 (HCW) 感染高后果病原体,凸显了感染预防和控制 (IPC) 方面持续存在的差距。我们评估了埃塞俄比亚亚的斯亚贝巴受感染医护人员的 IPC 依从性及其决定因素,为未来的 暴发 准备工作提供信息。方法 这项基于人口普查的横断面研究(2020 年 3 月至 2021 年 3 月)评估了 1152 名感染 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的医护人员,他们在 诊断 发生前 14 天有临床暴露。通过改编的 OSHA 金字塔将环境分为:高病原体指定区域隔离和 治疗 单位、一般高风险区域 [重症监护室、急诊科和手术室]、中风险临床区域 [住院和门诊部门] 和低风险支持区域 [行政和非临床区域]。遵守被定义为在超过 50% 的互动中采取正确的做法。双变量卡方检验和多变量逻辑回归确定了穿/脱 (n = 742) 和 N95 密封检查 (n = 350) 的独立决定因素,报告调整后的比值比 (aOR),P 结果置信区间为 95% 只有 19.2% 的感染医护人员在高病原体指定区域工作。口罩 (85.7-97.7%) 和手套 (68.2-98.0%) 的依从性很高,但长袍、工作服、头帽和鞋套的依从性低于 50%。例外情况包括面罩/护目镜 (52.8%) 和在气溶胶产生程序 (AGP) 期间使用 N95 (66.5%)。N95 密封检查合规率为 34.9%;只有 1.1% 使用经过适合性测试的呼吸器。手部卫生的比例从接触前的 49.3% 上升到接触液体后的 82.5%。卡方分析将医疗保健专业人员和高病原体指定区域状态与显着优越的依从性联系起来。对于穿/脱,非高病原体指定区域放置(一般高风险区域 aOR = 0.12 (0.07-0.19);中风险临床区域 aOR = 0.08 (0.04-0.14);低风险支持区域 [aOR = 0.07 (0.03-0.17)] 和支持人员 [aOR = 0.35 (0.14-0.88)];AGP 参与 [aOR = 3.61 (2.33-5.58)] 和 IPC 训练 [aOR = 1.59 (1.05-2.41)] 是一般高风险区域中的阳性预测因子 aOR = 0.53 (0.30-0.93);aOR = 0.33 (0.16-0.66);低风险支持区域 [aOR = 0.25 (0.08-0.77)]。阳性预测因子包括公共生活 [aOR = 2.37 (1.29-4.35)]、IPC 培训 [aOR = 1.71 (1.03-2.83)] 和 AGP 参与 [aOR = 1.71 (1.05-2.80)],而年龄 > 30 [aOR = 0.57 (0.34-0.98)] 和压力 [aOR = 0.46(0.28-0.77)]是负决定因素。结论 这项研究强调了医护人员之间的 IPC 差距,特别是在大多数感染发生的非指定区域,强调了所有医疗环境中标准化 IPC 的必要性。

papers.title: A qualitative study to assess lived experience of patients with COVID-19 at tertiary care hospital, Uttarakhand
papers.abstract: Background: Most people infected with the COVID-19 virus faced physical symptoms like mild to moderate respiratory distress but recover without requiring special treatment and also experienced psychosocial barriers like fear stress and stigma related to this pandemic. Methods: A Phenomenological study for COVID-19 positive patients was conducted during 2nd outbreak of COVID-19 at tertiary care hospital. Purposive sampling technique (maximum variance) was employed to collect information from COVID-19 patients admitted in COVID-19 isolation ward. Sample size was based upon data saturation which was achieved after 8 interviews. Participant’s inclusion criteria as aged above 18 years, one COVID-19 positive report by RT-PCR method and admitted in IPD. Questionnaire was administered through WhatsApp video call using ‘cube call recorder’ and it will be recoded with consent of the patient for the purpose of assessing data validity at later stage of research. Ethical permission was obtained from research review board of the institute. Results: Patients admitted in COVID-19 ward narrates mixed emotions of physical parameters health like severe body ache, respiratory problems like dyspnea, fever, weakness and cough as well psychological stress, tension and fear of loss of life. Opposed to this study our study participants narrate that doctors and nurses assist patients in their daily activity of living like provide timely medication food and warm water and assists during urination and defecation as patients unable to do so. But patients were experienced marginalization due VIP culture in the ward and hospital. Conclusions: Patients with COVID-19 experienced physical as well as psychosocial issues during hospitalization and at home due to lack of COVID-19 related information.
papers.journal: International Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to assess the lived experience of patients with COVID-19 at a tertiary care hospital in Uttarakhand, focusing on both physical symptoms and psychosocial barriers they faced during the pandemic.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study employed a phenomenological approach, using purposive sampling (maximum variance) to collect data from patients admitted in the isolation ward. Data saturation was achieved after 8 interviews, and the questionnaire was administered via WhatsApp video call with consent for data validation. Ethical permission was obtained from the research review board.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Patients with COVID-19 experienced a range of physical symptoms including severe body ache, respiratory problems like dyspnea, fever, weakness, and cough, as well as psychological stress, tension, and fear of mortality. Despite these challenges, healthcare providers offered support through timely medication, food, and assistance with daily activities. However, patients also reported marginalization due to the VIP culture in the hospital.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights a lack of consistent information about the disease, which may have contributed to psychological stress. There is no explicit mention of how these findings compare to other SARS-CoV-2 variants or other populations, leaving some evidence gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a need for improved communication and information dissemination about COVID-19 to reduce psychosocial stress among patients. Additionally, addressing the VIP culture in hospitals to prevent marginalization of patients is recommended.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explores the lived experience of patients with COVID-19 at a tertiary care hospital in Uttarakhand, focusing on their physical and psychosocial challenges. The research used a phenomenological approach with purposive sampling, achieving data saturation after 8 interviews. Participants reported mixed emotions, including severe physical symptoms and psychological stress, but also noted support from healthcare providers. However, they experienced marginalization due to the VIP culture in the hospital. The study emphasizes the need for better information dissemination and addressing systemic issues in healthcare settings to improve patient experiences.

papers.title: Structural stability and functional changes of the cognitive style of empathizing-systemizing in university students at late adolescence: A study used fixed-point observations data including the COVID-19 pandemic period.
papers.abstract: Cognitive styles are individuals' approaches to cognitive activities. This study examined the stability and variation of a cognitive style of empathizing-systemizing (E-S) among university students in late adolescence. Anonymous questionnaire surveys for second-year university students were conducted in October at 2011, 2014, 2017, and 2021, although E-S function was not analyzed for 2011. The number of valid data at each year ranged 469-480 in men and 420-432 in women. To examine the stability and variation, simultaneous multi-group analyses were conducted by gender. The stability and variation of E-S structure over the study period were examined by comparing structures of subfactors of empathizing and systemizing. Changes of E-S function were examined by analyzing the effects of E-S on mental distress through cognitive appraisal/coping processes under stressful situations. As the results, the structure of E-S was found stable across all study points in the sense of configural invariance in both men and women, even under the COVID-19 pandemic. E-S function shown clearly effected on mental distress. The function of E-S was also generally maintained, although several minor variations were observed during the entire study period.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the stability and variation of the empathizing-systemizing (E-S) cognitive style in university students during late adolescence, focusing on structural invariance and functional changes over time, including the COVID-19 pandemic period.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study employed anonymous questionnaire surveys conducted in October of 2011, 2014, 2017, and 2021 among second-year university students, with valid data ranging from 469 to 480 in men and 420 to 432 in women per year. Simultaneous multi-group analyses by gender were performed to assess the stability and variation of E-S structure and function.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The structure of the empathizing-systemizing (E-S) cognitive style demonstrated configural invariance across all study points in both men and women, including during the COVID-19 pandemic. The E-S function significantly influenced mental distress through cognitive appraisal and coping processes under stressful situations, and its function was generally maintained despite minor variations over the study period.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in E-S structure or function across different demographic subgroups beyond gender. The study does not address potential confounding factors such as socioeconomic status, academic pressure, or pre-existing mental health conditions that may influence E-S stability or its impact on mental distress.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should investigate the mechanisms underlying the observed stability of E-S structure and the role of E-S function in mental distress, particularly during prolonged stressors like pandemics. Longitudinal studies incorporating broader demographic and contextual variables are needed to validate these findings and explore their applicability to other populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study assessed the stability and variation of the empathizing-systemizing (E-S) cognitive style in university students during late adolescence, using multi-year questionnaire surveys (2011, 2014, 2017, 2021) with sample sizes ranging from 469 to 480 in men and 420 to 432 in women. Structural invariance of E-S was confirmed across all time points, including the COVID-19 pandemic period, while its function significantly influenced mental distress through cognitive processes. Minor variations in E-S function were observed, but its overall role remained consistent. The findings highlight the resilience of E-S structure and its potential impact on mental health, though gaps remain regarding demographic heterogeneity and confounding factors.

papers.title: Health outcomes and social determinants in people living with HIV in Sweden : insights from the COVID-19 era and beyond
papers.abstract: People with HIV (PWH) experience improved health and quality of life in the era of contemporary antiretroviral treatment (ART), and their life expectancy in high- income countries approaches that of people without HIV. However, disparities remain. PWH have been shown to face an increased risk and earlier onset of age- related comorbidities, even with access to effective ART and viral suppression. The comorbidity burden has been attributed in part to long-term effects of life- long ART and to residual low-grade inflammation and immune dysfunction that persist despite ART. Furthermore, PWH in high-income countries such as Sweden have lower socioeconomic status, including lower education and income, and approximately 60% are migrants. These social determinants are themselves associated with a higher risk of age-related comorbidities and may contribute to the excess risk observed among PWH. The extent to which these social factors contribute, however, has been less well studied and is important to clarify in order to target interventions effectively. The overall aim of the thesis was to investigate the risk of comorbidities, with a focus on COVID-19 and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), in PWH compared with people without HIV. Through linkage of Swedish nationwide registers across four studies, these outcomes were examined in virtually the entire adult Swedish population or a sample of it, while accounting for demographics, socioeconomic factors, and underlying comorbidities. Study I assessed the risk of severe COVID-19 (intensive care admission or mortality) among individuals hospitalised with COVID-19 by HIV status during the first phase of the pandemic (February 2020 to October 2021). In total, 64,815 individuals were hospitalised with COVID-19, of whom 121 were PWH. Odds ratios (OR) were estimated using logistic regression. The unadjusted OR of severe COVID-19 was lower among PWH compared with people without HIV (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.34-0.94), whereas adjustment for age and sex showed no significant difference (adjOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.43-1.26). These findings added to the evidence that PWH with access to ART, viral suppression, and a high CD4+ T-cell count did not have a higher risk of severe COVID-19 than people without HIV. The lower unadjusted OR was largely explained by PWH being younger at admission, possibly reflecting a different clinical threshold for admission rather than a true difference in COVID-19 severity. Study II investigated the risk of COVID-19 hospitalisation following confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in PWH (n=1,348) compared with people without HIV (n=1,669,389) between January 2021 and February 2023. Analyses were categorised by vaccination status and by pandemic period (pre-Omicron, Omicron during public testing, and Omicron after public testing) and ORs were estimated using logistic regression. Among those unvaccinated or vaccinated with only two doses, unadjusted ORs were significantly increased in PWH compared with people without HIV, but not after adjustment for age, sex, month of SARS-CoV-2 infection, income, migrant status, and comorbidities. No significant differences were observed among those vaccinated with at least three doses. During Omicron and public testing, PWH had significantly increased adjusted odds of hospitalisation compared with people without HIV. Taken together, the risk of COVID-19 hospitalisation in PWH was overall similar to that of people without HIV, although temporal variations were observed and may reflect differences in testing patterns by HIV status. Study III estimated the risk ratio (RR) of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination uptake across doses 1-5 using modified Poisson regression, among individuals alive and resident in Sweden at the start of vaccination, comparing PWH (n=7,668) with people without HIV (n=8,168,340). People with HIV were divided into two groups based on COVID-19 vaccination prioritisation: non-vulnerable PWH and clinically vulnerable PWH. In both groups, PWH had lower unadjusted 3-dose uptake (non- vulnerable: RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.88-0.91); however, after adjustment, particularly for country of birth, PWH had higher uptake (non-vulnerable: adjRR 1.17, 95% CI 1.15-1.19). This pattern did not persist among individuals aged ≥65 years, where 5-dose uptake was lower among non-vulnerable PWH (adjRR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85- 0.96). Taken together, PWH had lower vaccination uptake than people without HIV, although it was mainly explained by the higher proportion of PWH born outside Sweden. At the same time, the higher adjusted uptake among PWH underscores that frequent healthcare contact that comes with living with HIV facilitates vaccination, however the same advantage did not appear to extend to older PWH. This further suggests that public health measures addressing vaccination uptake should be directed at migrant populations rather than at PWH. Study IV assessed the risk of severe renal events, cardiovascular events, and all- cause mortality following a T2DM diagnosis in PWH (n=350) compared with people without HIV (n=311,668) between 2010 and 2024. Hazard ratios (HR) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for quintiles of a propensity score based on age, sex, migrant status, comorbidities, and socioeconomic status. A significantly increased risk of major adverse kidney events among PWH compared with people without HIV (adjHR 2.04, 95% CI 1.57- 2.65) was found. No significant differences were observed for major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality in multivariable models. The renal signal persisted across several sensitivity analyses, however, correction for the known benign serum creatinine increase associated with bictegravir, cobicistat, dolutegravir, and rilpivirine attenuated the estimate and did not remain statistically significant (adjHR 1.32, 95% CI 0.90-1.94). Although detailed exploration of ART was limited by the few events among PWH, these findings highlight the importance of closer monitoring and careful management of renal risk factors in PWH with T2DM and warrant further research to clarify this association. Study I-IV collectively highlight that the previously observed increased comorbidity risk among PWH may be shaped not only by biological vulnerability and ART, but also by social determinants and differences in healthcare access and monitoring. Consequently, the excess comorbidity burden among PWH may be meaningfully reduced by addressing sociodemographic disparities, optimising comorbidity management, and strengthening preventive care, while further research continues to explore the underlying mechanisms and improve risk prediction. source_records.abstract: People with HIV (PWH) experience improved health and quality of life in the era of contemporary antiretroviral treatment (ART), and their life expectancy in high- income countries approaches that of people without HIV. However, disparities remain. PWH have been shown to face an increased risk and earlier onset of age- related comorbidities, even with access to effective ART and viral suppression. The comorbidity burden has been attributed in part to long-term effects of life- long ART and to residual low-grade inflammation and immune dysfunction that persist despite ART. Furthermore, PWH in high-income countries such as Sweden have lower socioeconomic status, including lower education and income, and approximately 60% are migrants. These social determinants are themselves associated with a higher risk of age-related comorbidities and may contribute to the excess risk observed among PWH. The extent to which these social factors contribute, however, has been less well studied and is important to clarify in order to target interventions effectively. The overall aim of the thesis was to investigate the risk of comorbidities, with a focus on COVID-19 and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), in PWH compared with people without HIV. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed persistent disparities in health outcomes among people with HIV (PWH) despite effective antiretroviral therapy, focusing on the contribution of social determinants and the impact of COVID-19. It aimed to clarify how socioeconomic factors influence the excess risk of age-related comorbidities and COVID-19 outcomes in PWH compared with people without HIV.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Four nationwide register-based studies were conducted in Sweden using linked data from virtually the entire adult population or large samples. Study I included 64,815 individuals hospitalised with COVID-19 (121 PWH) from February 2020 to October 2021. Study II compared 1,348 PWH with 1,669,389 people without HIV for COVID-19 hospitalisation from January 2021 to February 2023. Study III assessed COVID-19 vaccination uptake among 7,668 PWH and 8,168,340 people without HIV. Study IV evaluated renal, cardiovascular events, and mortality after type 2 diabetes diagnosis in 350 PWH versus 311,668 people without HIV (2010–2024).
analysis.methods: Odds ratios (OR) and hazard ratios (HR) were estimated using logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models, respectively. Analyses adjusted for demographics, socioeconomic factors, comorbidities, and vaccination status. Study II stratified by vaccination status and pandemic period (pre-Omicron, Omicron during public testing, Omicron after public testing). Study III used modified Poisson regression to estimate risk ratios for vaccination uptake.
analysis.main_results: In Study I, the unadjusted OR for severe COVID-19 was lower in PWH (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.34–0.94), but adjustment for age and sex eliminated the difference (adjOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.43–1.26). Study II found increased unadjusted ORs for COVID-19 hospitalisation in unvaccinated or twice-vaccinated PWH, but not after adjustment; during Omicron with public testing, adjusted ORs were significantly higher in PWH. Study III showed lower unadjusted 3-dose vaccination uptake in PWH (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.88–0.91), but higher adjusted uptake (adjRR 1.17, 95% CI 1.15–1.19), except in those aged ≥65 years (adjRR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.96). Study IV reported a significantly increased risk of major adverse kidney events in PWH with T2DM (adjHR 2.04, 95% CI 1.57–2.65).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that PWH with access to ART and viral suppression do not have a higher risk of severe COVID-19 than people without HIV, though temporal variations during Omicron highlight potential testing biases. Lower vaccination uptake in PWH appears largely explained by migrant status, while frequent healthcare contact may facilitate vaccination except in older PWH. The increased risk of renal events in PWH with T2DM underscores the need for targeted monitoring.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that addressing socioeconomic disparities, particularly among migrant populations, may reduce excess comorbidity risks in PWH. Enhanced renal monitoring is warranted in PWH with T2DM. Vaccination programs should prioritise migrant groups to improve uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Detailed exploration of antiretroviral therapy effects was limited by few events among PWH, constraining causal inference. The register-based design may introduce residual confounding and misclassification. Despite these limitations, the nationwide scope and adjustment for multiple confounders strengthen the evidence, warranting moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis investigated health outcomes among people with HIV (PWH) in Sweden, focusing on COVID-19 severity, hospitalisation, vaccination uptake, and renal/cardiovascular risks after type 2 diabetes diagnosis. Using nationwide register data, four studies compared PWH with people without HIV. Severe COVID-19 risk was similar after adjustment, though unadjusted differences reflected younger age at admission. COVID-19 hospitalisation risk varied by vaccination status and pandemic period, with higher adjusted odds during Omicron with public testing. Vaccination uptake was lower in PWH before adjustment but higher after accounting for migrant status, except in those aged ≥65 years. PWH with T2DM had a twofold increased risk of major adverse kidney events. The findings highlight the role of socioeconomic factors in health disparities and support targeted interventions, including improved renal monitoring and vaccination strategies for migrant populations.

analysis_en.main_results: In Study I, the unadjusted OR for severe COVID-19 was lower in PWH (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.34–0.94), but adjustment for age and sex eliminated the difference (adjOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.43–1.26). Study II found increased unadjusted ORs for COVID-19 hospitalisation in unvaccinated or twice-vaccinated PWH, but not after adjustment; during Omicron with public testing, adjusted ORs were significantly higher in PWH. Study III showed lower unadjusted 3-dose vaccination uptake in PWH (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.88–0.91), but higher adjusted uptake (adjRR 1.17, 95% CI 1.15–1.19), except in those aged ≥65 years (adjRR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85–0.96). Study IV reported a significantly increased risk of major adverse kidney events in PWH with T2DM (adjHR 2.04, 95% CI 1.57–2.65).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that PWH with access to ART and viral suppression do not have a higher risk of severe COVID-19 than people without HIV, though temporal variations during Omicron highlight potential testing biases. Lower vaccination uptake in PWH appears largely explained by migrant status, while frequent healthcare contact may facilitate vaccination except in older PWH. The increased risk of renal events in PWH with T2DM underscores the need for targeted monitoring.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that addressing socioeconomic disparities, particularly among migrant populations, may reduce excess comorbidity risks in PWH. Enhanced renal monitoring is warranted in PWH with T2DM. Vaccination programs should prioritise migrant groups to improve uptake.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Detailed exploration of antiretroviral therapy effects was limited by few events among PWH, constraining causal inference. The register-based design may introduce residual confounding and misclassification. Despite these limitations, the nationwide scope and adjustment for multiple confounders strengthen the evidence, warranting moderate confidence.

papers.title_zh: Health outcomes and social determinants in people living with HIV in Sweden : insights from the COVID-19 era and beyond
papers.source_body_en: People with HIV (PWH) experience improved health and quality of life in the era of contemporary antiretroviral treatment (ART), and their life expectancy in high- income countries approaches that of people without HIV. However, disparities remain. PWH have been shown to face an increased risk and earlier onset of age- related comorbidities, even with access to effective ART and viral suppression. The comorbidity burden has been attributed in part to long-term effects of life- long ART and to residual low-grade inflammation and immune dysfunction that persist despite ART. Furthermore, PWH in high-income countries such as Sweden have lower socioeconomic status, including lower education and income, and approximately 60% are migrants. These social determinants are themselves associated with a higher risk of age-related comorbidities and may contribute to the excess risk observed among PWH. The extent to which these social factors contribute, however, has been less well studied and is important to clarify in order to target interventions effectively. The overall aim of the thesis was to investigate the risk of comorbidities, with a focus on COVID-19 and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), in PWH compared with people without HIV. Through linkage of Swedish nationwide registers across four studies, these outcomes were examined in virtually the entire adult Swedish population or a sample of it, while accounting for demographics, socioeconomic factors, and underlying comorbidities. Study I assessed the risk of severe COVID-19 (intensive care admission or mortality) among individuals hospitalised with COVID-19 by HIV status during the first phase of the pandemic (February 2020 to October 2021). In total, 64,815 individuals were hospitalised with COVID-19, of whom 121 were PWH. Odds ratios (OR) were estimated using logistic regression. The unadjusted OR of severe COVID-19 was lower among PWH compared with people without HIV (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.34-0.94), whereas adjustment for age and sex showed no significant difference (adjOR 0.70, 95% CI 0.43-1.26). These findings added to the evidence that PWH with access to ART, viral suppression, and a high CD4+ T-cell count did not have a higher risk of severe COVID-19 than people without HIV. The lower unadjusted OR was largely explained by PWH being younger at admission, possibly reflecting a different clinical threshold for admission rather than a true difference in COVID-19 severity. Study II investigated the risk of COVID-19 hospitalisation following confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in PWH (n=1,348) compared with people without HIV (n=1,669,389) between January 2021 and February 2023. Analyses were categorised by vaccination status and by pandemic period (pre-Omicron, Omicron during public testing, and Omicron after public testing) and ORs were estimated using logistic regression. Among those unvaccinated or vaccinated with only two doses, unadjusted ORs were significantly increased in PWH compared with people without HIV, but not after adjustment for age, sex, month of SARS-CoV-2 infection, income, migrant status, and comorbidities. No significant differences were observed among those vaccinated with at least three doses. During Omicron and public testing, PWH had significantly increased adjusted odds of hospitalisation compared with people without HIV. Taken together, the risk of COVID-19 hospitalisation in PWH was overall similar to that of people without HIV, although temporal variations were observed and may reflect differences in testing patterns by HIV status. Study III estimated the risk ratio (RR) of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination uptake across doses 1-5 using modified Poisson regression, among individuals alive and resident in Sweden at the start of vaccination, comparing PWH (n=7,668) with people without HIV (n=8,168,340). People with HIV were divided into two groups based on COVID-19 vaccination prioritisation: non-vulnerable PWH and clinically vulnerable PWH. In both groups, PWH had lower unadjusted 3-dose uptake (non- vulnerable: RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.88-0.91); however, after adjustment, particularly for country of birth, PWH had higher uptake (non-vulnerable: adjRR 1.17, 95% CI 1.15-1.19). This pattern did not persist among individuals aged ≥65 years, where 5-dose uptake was lower among non-vulnerable PWH (adjRR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85- 0.96). Taken together, PWH had lower vaccination uptake than people without HIV, although it was mainly explained by the higher proportion of PWH born outside Sweden. At the same time, the higher adjusted uptake among PWH underscores that frequent healthcare contact that comes with living with HIV facilitates vaccination, however the same advantage did not appear to extend to older PWH. This further suggests that public health measures addressing vaccination uptake should be directed at migrant populations rather than at PWH. Study IV assessed the risk of severe renal events, cardiovascular events, and all- cause mortality following a T2DM diagnosis in PWH (n=350) compared with people without HIV (n=311,668) between 2010 and 2024. Hazard ratios (HR) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for quintiles of a propensity score based on age, sex, migrant status, comorbidities, and socioeconomic status. A significantly increased risk of major adverse kidney events among PWH compared with people without HIV (adjHR 2.04, 95% CI 1.57- 2.65) was found. No significant differences were observed for major adverse cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality in multivariable models. The renal signal persisted across several sensitivity analyses, however, correction for the known benign serum creatinine increase associated with bictegravir, cobicistat, dolutegravir, and rilpivirine attenuated the estimate and did not remain statistically significant (adjHR 1.32, 95% CI 0.90-1.94). Although detailed exploration of ART was limited by the few events among PWH, these findings highlight the importance of closer monitoring and careful management of renal risk factors in PWH with T2DM and warrant further research to clarify this association. Study I-IV collectively highlight that the previously observed increased comorbidity risk among PWH may be shaped not only by biological vulnerability and ART, but also by social determinants and differences in healthcare access and monitoring. Consequently, the excess comorbidity burden among PWH may be meaningfully reduced by addressing sociodemographic disparities, optimising comorbidity management, and strengthening preventive care, while further research continues to explore the underlying mechanisms and improve risk prediction. analysis_zh.methods: 分别使用逻辑回归和 Cox 比例风险模型估计优势比 (OR) 和风险比 (HR)。根据人口统计、社会经济因素、合并症和 疫苗接种 状态进行调整的分析。研究 II 按 疫苗接种 状态和大流行时期(Omicron 之前、公开测试期间的 Omicron、公开测试后的 Omicron)进行分层。研究 III 使用修正的泊松回归来估计 疫苗接种 摄取的风险比。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,解决社会经济差异,特别是移民人口中的社会经济差异,可能会降低艾滋病毒感染者过度合并症的风险。对于患有 T2DM 的 PWH,需要加强肾脏监测。疫苗接种 计划应优先考虑移民群体,以提高吸收率。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 抗逆转录病毒治疗效果的详细探索受到感染者中少数事件的限制,限制了因果推断。基于寄存器的设计可能会引入残余混杂和错误分类。尽管存在这些限制,但全国范围和对多种混杂因素的调整增强了证据,值得适度的信心。

papers.title: Measuring and removing near-duplicate contamination in alignment-free SARS-CoV-2 lineage classification benchmarks
papers.abstract: Alignment-free lineage assignment from k-mer frequency profiles is widely used for SARS-CoV-2 surveillance, and the methods that do it are ranked against each other by margins of one or two percentage points. Those rankings rest on an unchecked protocol. Public repositories hold many near-duplicate genomes, and stratified random splitting puts members of such a group on both sides of the split, so a classifier is credited for sequences it has already seen. This study measures the effect and offers a remedy. We propose quantised profile hashing, which finds near duplicates directly in k-mer feature space by rounding each frequency vector and hashing it. No sequence is compared with any other, so one pass over the feature matrix suffices and no similarity threshold has to be chosen. Rounding is also what makes the groups well defined, and they are then kept whole across the training, validation and test sets. On 255,611 genomes from seven Pango lineages, random splitting leaves 5.09% of test sequences with a near duplicate in training, as large as the margins separating published methods. Ten update rules were then trained twice, identically except for the partition. The contaminated benchmark separates one rule from the leader at 0.05; the clean one separates none. The two orderings are uncorrelated, Kendall tau = +0.022, with rules moving 3.2 positions on average and the leader of one benchmark ranking eighth on the other. A ranking obtained under contamination therefore says nothing about the ranking without it, and the quantity worth reporting beside a score is the leakage rate of the split.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Alignment-free lineage assignment using k-mer frequency profiles is widely used for SARS-CoV-2 surveillance, yet benchmark rankings of these methods rely on protocols that have not been validated for contamination risks. The study highlights that public repositories contain many near-duplicate genomes, which can inflate apparent classifier performance when stratified random splitting inadvertently places duplicates across training and test sets.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluates the impact of near-duplicate contamination in SARS-CoV-2 lineage classification benchmarks using 255,611 genomes spanning seven Pango lineages. It compares benchmark rankings under contaminated and clean data splits, training ten update rules identically except for the partition method.
analysis.methods: The authors propose quantised profile hashing to detect near duplicates directly in k-mer feature space by rounding frequency vectors and hashing them, ensuring groups are kept intact across training, validation, and test sets. This approach avoids pairwise comparisons and eliminates the need to choose a similarity threshold.
analysis.main_results: Under random splitting, 5.09% of test sequences had a near duplicate in training, comparable to the margins separating published methods. The contaminated benchmark separated one rule from the leader at 0.05, while the clean benchmark separated none. Rankings under contamination and clean conditions were uncorrelated (Kendall tau = +0.022), with rules moving an average of 3.2 positions and the leader of one benchmark ranking eighth on the other.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that contamination in benchmark datasets can produce misleading rankings of SARS-CoV-2 lineage classification methods. The proposed quantised profile hashing method provides a practical remedy by eliminating leakage between training and test sets, thereby enabling fairer comparisons.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work underscores the need to report leakage rates alongside benchmark scores to ensure transparency in SARS-CoV-2 surveillance method evaluations. It provides a reproducible framework for assessing lineage classification tools, which is critical for accurate public health surveillance and decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to SARS-CoV-2 lineage classification benchmarks and does not evaluate the impact of contamination on downstream epidemiological or clinical applications. The evidence strength is high for the specific methodological question addressed, but generalisability to other viruses or contexts remains untested.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of near-duplicate contamination in SARS-CoV-2 lineage classification benchmarks, where public repositories contain many near-identical genomes that can inflate classifier performance when stratified random splitting inadvertently places duplicates across training and test sets. Using 255,611 genomes from seven Pango lineages, the authors demonstrate that random splitting leaves 5.09% of test sequences with a near duplicate in training, comparable to the margins separating published methods. They propose quantised profile hashing, which detects near duplicates in k-mer feature space by rounding frequency vectors and hashing them, ensuring groups remain intact across partitions without pairwise comparisons or similarity thresholds. Under contamination, benchmark rankings separated one rule from the leader at 0.05, while clean benchmarks separated none, and rankings were uncorrelated (Kendall tau = +0.022), with rules moving an average of 3.2 positions. The findings reveal that contamination can produce misleading rankings, and the proposed method provides a practical remedy by eliminating leakage between training and test sets. The work highlights the need to report leakage rates alongside benchmark scores for transparency in SARS-CoV-2 surveillance method evaluations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 使用 k-mer 频率分布的无比对谱系分配广泛用于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 监测,但这些方法的基准排名依赖于尚未针对污染风险进行验证的协议。该研究强调,公共存储库包含许多近乎重复的 基因组,当分层随机分割无意中在训练和测试集中放置重复项时,这可能会夸大明显的分类器性能。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用跨越七个 Pango 谱系的 255,611 个 基因组 来评估 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 谱系分类基准中近乎重复污染的影响。它比较了污染数据和干净数据分割下的基准排名,除了分区方法之外,以相同的方式训练十个更新规则。
elements_zh.methods: 作者提出量化配置文件哈希,通过舍入频率 媒介 并对其进行哈希处理,直接在 k-mer 特征空间中检测接近的重复项,确保组在训练、验证和测试集中保持完整。这种方法避免了成对比较,并且无需选择相似性阈值。
elements_zh.main_results: 在随机分割下,5.09% 的测试序列在训练中几乎有重复,这与已发布方法之间的差距相当。受污染的基准测试将一条规则与领先规则的分离度为 0.05,而干净的基准测试则没有分离任何规则。污染和清洁条件下的排名不相关(Kendall tau = +0.022),规则平均移动 3.2 个位置,一个基准的领先者在另一个基准上排名第八。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,基准数据集中的污染可能会对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 谱系分类方法产生误导性的排名。所提出的量化配置文件哈希方法通过消除训练集和测试集之间的泄漏提供了一种实用的补救措施,从而实现更公平的比较。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项工作强调需要报告泄漏率和基准分数,以确保 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 监测 方法评估的透明度。它为评估谱系分类工具提供了一个可重复的框架,这对于准确的公共卫生 监测 和决策至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系分类基准,并未评估污染对下游流行病学或临床应用的影响。对于所解决的具体方法问题,证据强度很高,但对其他病毒或环境的普遍性尚未经过测试。

papers.abstract_zh: 来自 k 聚体频率分布的无比对谱系分配广泛用于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 监测,并且执行此操作的方法以一两个百分点的差距相互排名。这些排名基于未经检查的协议。公共存储库保存许多近乎重复的 基因组,并且分层随机分裂将此类组的成员置于分裂的两侧,因此分类器因其已经看到的序列而被记入。这项研究衡量了效果并提供了补救措施。我们提出量化配置文件哈希,它通过对每个频率 媒介 进行舍入并对其进行哈希处理,直接在 k-mer 特征空间中找到接近的重复项。没有序列与任何其他序列进行比较,因此只需传递一次特征矩阵就足够了,无需选择相似性阈值。舍入也是使组得到明确定义的原因,然后它们在训练、验证和测试集中保持完整。在来自 7 个 Pango 谱系的 255,611 个 基因组 上,随机分割使 5.09% 的测试序列在训练中几乎重复,与分隔已发布方法的边缘一样大。然后十个更新规则被训练两次,除了分区之外,其他规则都相同。受污染的基准将一条规则与领先规则分开 0.05;干净的人没有分离。这两个排序不相关,Kendall tau = +0.022,规则平均移动 3.2 个位置,一个基准的领先者在另一个基准上排名第八。因此,在污染下获得的排名并没有说明没有污染的排名,并且除了分数之外值得报告的数量是分裂的泄漏率。
papers.summary_zh: 来自 k 聚体频率分布的无比对谱系分配广泛用于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 监测,并且执行此操作的方法以一两个百分点的差距相互排名。这些排名基于未经检查的协议。公共存储库保存许多近乎重复的 基因组,并且分层随机分裂将此类组的成员置于分裂的两侧,因此分类器因其已经看到的序列而被记入。这项研究衡量了效果并提供了补救措施。我们提出量化配置文件哈希,它通过对每个频率 媒介 进行舍入并对其进行哈希处理,直接在 k-mer 特征空间中找到接近的重复项。没有序列与任何其他序列进行比较,因此只需传递一次特征矩阵就足够了,无需选择相似性阈值。舍入也是使组得到明确定义的原因,然后它们在训练、验证和测试集中保持完整。在来自 7 个 Pango 谱系的 255,611 个 基因组 上,随机分割使 5.09% 的测试序列在训练中几乎重复,与分隔已发布方法的边缘一样大。然后十个更新规则被训练两次,除了分区之外,其他规则都相同。受污染的基准将一条规则与领先规则分开 0.05;干净的人没有分离。这两个排序不相关,Kendall tau = +0.022,规则平均移动 3.2 个位置,一个基准的领先者在另一个基准上排名第八。因此,在污染下获得的排名并没有说明没有污染的排名,并且除了分数之外值得报告的数量是分裂的泄漏率。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 使用 k-mer 频率分布的无比对谱系分配广泛用于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 监测,但这些方法的基准排名依赖于尚未针对污染风险进行验证的协议。该研究强调,公共存储库包含许多近乎重复的 基因组,当分层随机分割无意中在训练和测试集中放置重复项时,这可能会夸大明显的分类器性能。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用跨越七个 Pango 谱系的 255,611 个 基因组 来评估 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 谱系分类基准中近乎重复污染的影响。它比较了污染数据和干净数据分割下的基准排名,除了分区方法之外,以相同的方式训练十个更新规则。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者提出量化配置文件哈希,通过舍入频率 媒介 并对其进行哈希处理,直接在 k-mer 特征空间中检测接近的重复项,确保组在训练、验证和测试集中保持完整。这种方法避免了成对比较,并且无需选择相似性阈值。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在随机分割下,5.09% 的测试序列在训练中几乎有重复,这与已发布方法之间的差距相当。受污染的基准测试将一条规则与领先规则的分离度为 0.05,而干净的基准测试则没有分离任何规则。污染和清洁条件下的排名不相关(Kendall tau = +0.022),规则平均移动 3.2 个位置,一个基准的领先者在另一个基准上排名第八。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,基准数据集中的污染可能会对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 谱系分类方法产生误导性的排名。所提出的量化配置文件哈希方法通过消除训练集和测试集之间的泄漏提供了一种实用的补救措施,从而实现更公平的比较。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项工作强调需要报告泄漏率和基准分数,以确保 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 监测 方法评估的透明度。它为评估谱系分类工具提供了一个可重复的框架,这对于准确的公共卫生 监测 和决策至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系分类基准,并未评估污染对下游流行病学或临床应用的影响。对于所解决的具体方法问题,证据强度很高,但对其他病毒或环境的普遍性尚未经过测试。
